# Business associate agreement (BAA) templates

Drafting aids for a future US engagement under HIPAA. No BAA has been signed for this project. HIPAA does not apply automatically to a Bangladesh clinic or to every health-related website, and EU or Bangladesh processor agreements need their own assessment.

Start from the HHS [sample business associate agreement provisions](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/covered-entities/sample-business-associate-agreement-provisions/index.html) and have counsel draft the final agreement for the specific engagement. Keep signed contracts in restricted storage, never in this repository.

## Applicability and execution checklist

| Item | Evidence required |
|---|---|
| Parties and roles | The actual legal entities, and the covered entity / business associate determination |
| Service and data | What PHI is created, received, stored or transmitted, including metadata and context |
| Vendor eligibility | The exact service, plan and region permit PHI, and a current agreement is available |
| Permitted uses | Defined purposes and restrictions |
| Safeguards | Applicable Security Rule obligations, shared responsibilities and actual controls |
| Incident reporting | Process, contacts, content and timelines consistent with law |
| Subcontractors | Matching downstream restrictions |
| Patient rights | Support for access, amendment and accounting of disclosures |
| Oversight | HHS access and contractual evidence |
| Termination | Breach remedies, return or destruction of data, protection of retained data |
| Execution | Authorized signatures, dates, scope and a review owner |

Do not assume CDN, email or support vendors are exempt: assess the actual data flow and whether context reveals health information. No production PHI is used until the agreement is signed and the controls pass. A BAA does not make an insecure application acceptable.

## Drafting worksheet

| Clause group | Terms to complete |
|---|---|
| Parties and scope | Covered entity, business associate, underlying service agreement, effective date, description of processing |
| Definitions | HIPAA definitions, aligned with the main contract |
| Permitted uses | Specific purposes, minimum necessary standard, prohibited secondary uses |
| Safeguards | Administrative, physical and technical obligations; shared responsibilities |
| Incidents | Contacts, notice content, cooperation, negotiated response times |
| Subcontractors | Required downstream terms and change process |
| Rights assistance | Access, amendment and accounting support with workable deadlines |
| Oversight | Regulatory access and agreed evidence process |
| Covered entity duties | Changes to notices, authorizations and restrictions |
| Breach and remedies | Termination rights, cure periods and remedies |
| End of service | Return or destruction, exceptions when infeasible, continuing protections, export format |
| Commercial terms | Liability, indemnity, governing law, precedence, disputes |
| Execution | Signatories, dates and storage location |

Operational deadlines (for example 24- or 72-hour incident notice) are negotiated terms, not statutory BAA requirements. Security commitments must match the vendor's actual evidence. Review agreements at onboarding, renewal and after material changes.
